data.title: Bitcoin wipes out $731M as election hopes fade: BTC’s next test is…
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] traders faced liquidations on both sides as prices surged and then erased the rally.

On the 4th of November, Bitcoin climbed from $75.7k to $81.2k, triggering $407.92 million in liquidations. Shorts accounted for $309.98 million of that total.

The reversal on the 5th of November brought another $323.54 million in liquidations, including $294.11 million in longs. Meanwhile, total crypto Market Capitalization fell $132.7 billion that day, bringing losses since the local peak to $149 billion.

Short-term bullish sentiment following the midterm election results was immediately overrun by an equities market pullback, with major AI stocks coming under selling pressure.

Bitcoin volume trends show crypto isn’t exhausted, merely reactive

In a post on X, Glassnode observed that crypto traders are still here, despite the past month’s price retrace from $87k. Bitcoin [BTC] volume was at its lowest since 2023, before the August rally from $60k commenced.

Thereafter, volume remained above the August levels, which underlined sustained interest from traders and investors.

Rather than being a market collapse, the recent sell-off might be part of a healthy correction. Crypto intelligence platform Santiment posted that the crypto crowd became optimistic following the election results on the 4th of November.

This was a surprise, evidenced by the amount of short liquidations. Fueled by liquidations and FOMO, BTC briefly climbed past $81k.

Short-term FUD in reaction to selling in traditional markets across the globe sparked the Bitcoin reset. In both instances, the price went against the crowd’s expectations, showing why retail trader sentiment extremes can be counter-signals.

Bitcoin slips below key support level

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. wrote that the short liquidations reached the highest levels since late September. The Binance heist has also severely affected sentiment.

Since July, short-term holder BTC supply has expanded by 600k. It highlighted coins changing hands from long-term investors to newer market participants, and can also signal increased sensitivity to short-term price trends.

The True Market Mean was at $77.6k, and the brief foray above this level did not last. The metric measures the average cost basis of active investors while filtering out lost, dormant, or long-inactive coins.

A price slip below the TMM implied cooling market conditions and left investors at a loss on average. It could be a warning sign of a deeper correction.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin crowd expectations were punished over the past two days, leading to heavy liquidations and high volatility.
  • The volume trends were not comparable to the August slump, but losing the TMM suggested the market has reverted from bullish expansion to value-accumulation conditions.

data.title: PEARL integrates with NEAR Intents to expand cross-chain access for AI miners — Can demand follow?
data.description:
Pearl, the native token of the Pearl Layer-1 network, has launched on NEAR Intents. The move allows for swapping of tokens across more than 35 different networks. Additionally, the integration provides the Near Protocol’s [NEAR] Click API.

As a result, this makes it possible for wallets and applications to integrate Pearl [PEARL] token swaps.

In simple words, through NEAR’s infrastructure, miners will be able to swap PEARL for assets within all of those 35+ networks. Therefore, there may be easier access to stablecoins or other currencies for miners as they pay for electricity and hardware.

More importantly, Pearl’s Proof of Useful Work model links token issuance to AI computations that also secure the network. As such, miners receive both block rewards and inference fees based upon the same workload they are using to mine blocks.

This link could create a direct relationship between AI usage and token utility. However, for PEARL to have sustained value, it will require consistent AI-related workloads creating sufficient activity and generating fees that can support miners.

PEARL gains cross-chain access

As part of the integration, NEAR intents provides PEARL with access to an existing cross-chain market. No additional cross-chain bridges for each individual network would be required for this.

Currently, NEAR intents’ ecosystem provides a cross-chain marketplace that includes approximately 38 networks, along with more than 200 assets. Major stablecoin markets are included in the asset list as well.

This is important for miners who need to have liquid means to exit transactions quickly in order to meet costs associated with electricity and hardware. NEAR intents reported more than $37 billion in cumulative volume and more than $144 million in daily volume traded.

A large trading platform like this offers stability for those looking to utilize cross-chain swaps.

Moreover, confidential transactions enable users to transfer funds anonymously. Although the fact that the entire network is utilizing this function does not necessarily mean that there will be a greater demand for PEARL.

Instead, it will rely upon how frequently miners and traders utilize these services to conduct swaps, develop deeper liquidity levels, and ensure reliable execution.

Can AI demand sustain PEARL’s value?

PEARL’s next challenge is converting wider access into sustained market demand. PEARL’s market activity will show whether easier cross-chain access translates into genuine demand. At press time, the token was trading around $1.69, up 17% in the last 24 hours.

The daily volume increased alongside price rally, hovering near $12 million and was up 36%.

However, activity remains concentrated on a few centralized exchanges, suggesting NEAR access has yet to reshape its liquidity. This matters because GPU miners need reliable markets to convert rewards into operating funds.

Ultimately, stronger demand must therefore come from real AI workloads and paid inference, not token issuance alone.

Final Summary

data.title: ApeChain migrates to Chainlink CCIP for APE and USDC transfers – Details
data.description:
ApeChain is replacing LayerZero with Chainlink CCIP. This move comes as the layer 3 blockchain aims to strengthen its infrastructure and improve connectivity across the Yuga Labs ecosystem.

The migration makes CCIP the official cross-chain standard for ApeChain, Bored Ape Yacht Club applications, and APE.

Additionally, it will be migrating the ChainLink Cross-Chain Token (CCT) that is used by the CCT implementation of APE and USD Coin [USDC], among others. This is to enable programmable transfers from these tokens without having to use LayerZero’s former OFT.

Therefore, this may provide easier access to the decentralized application and community space across the Ethereum [ETH], Arbitrum, Base, and Polygon chains. As well, Chainlink has described CCIP as a single secure cross-chain standard.

Chainlink CCIP expands its reach

The expanded reach of Chainlink CCIP provides a larger scale significance for the ApeChain integration. Chainlink CCIP processes over $25 billion in cumulative transfer volume.

It also currently supports 60 to 77 different networks and has sent over 1.63 million messages. Previously, it was integrated with BitGo’s WBTC, Wyoming’s FRNT, and other assets from Kelp and Mantle.

These previous integrations have moved over $15 billion worth of token value via CCIP in 2026. In addition to providing additional support to this expanding network of users, Yuga Labs will also bring a large, consumer-focused, and NFT-centered ecosystem into play.

Ultimately, Rising transfers, repeat activity, deeper liquidity, and competitive fees will show whether adoption delivers lasting growth.

Can CCIP turn adoption into lasting demand?

While CCIP is continuing to expand its reach, it needs to continue translating this reach into sustainable revenue. More importantly, CCIP recently underwent its first upgrade (CCIP 2.0) since September 2026.

Additionally, integrations with Aave [AAVE], Lombard, and Venus demonstrate CCIP’s continued involvement in the development of DeFi. While CCIP continues to add to its involvement in DeFi infrastructure, commercial returns for the project remain limited.

This gap represents the difficulty in transitioning from simply being involved in infrastructure adoption into generating consistent economic returns.

Final Summary

data.title: XRP Ledger closes loophole that could let token burners mint new supply
data.description:
The XRP Ledger has activated the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment to close a security loophole in its permission delegation system.

Previously, an account given permission to burn tokens could also create new tokens under certain conditions. The fix blocks this unless the account also has permission to mint tokens.

The amendment also introduced fixes across several network features. These included Single Asset Vaults, lending, automated market makers (AMMs), the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs), NFTs and escrow. Other fixes covered sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation.

Why are these fixes required in the first place?

These fixes are mainly designed to address technical issues involving asset calculations, token transfers, liquidity pool operations, account permissions, and reserve requirements. For example, the AMM fix would now prevent liquidity providers from losing their pool tokens due to rounding errors during certain clawback operations.

Similarly, improvements to lending and vault operations would now result in accurate accounting and asset management. The update also boosts MPT transaction validation and resolves issues that could cause NFT offers to fail. All in all, the amendment aims to improve the reliability, security, and functionality of the XRP Ledger’s existing financial infrastructure. 

That said, its activation followed two weeks of uninterrupted validator support, as XRPL amendments required more than 80% approval from trusted validators.

XRP Ledger market footprint

This comes as the XRP Ledger ranks ninth among networks in the RWA League Table, with $644.6 million in distributed tokenized assets, representing a 29.20% increase over the past month.

This followed a recent report from AMBCrypto, which indicated that XRPL ranked 10th in tokenized assets, with $642.5 million just a week ago.

Meanwhile, Santiment’s data for XRP Ledger suggests that its Total Open Interest fell from approximately $1.3 billion to below $1 billion towards the end of October. However, it subsequently witnessed a sharp recovery, reaching approximately $1.15 billion at press time.

At the same time, the Stablecoin Supply Ratio stood at 31.31 at the time of writing, marking a decline from around 34.5 to below 30 before recovering. 

Final Summary

  • The amendment came in with a series of fixes across ten areas of the network.
  • This came in after two weeks of uninterrupted validator support.

data.title: TRUMP crashes 17% as Democrats sweep the midterms – $1.22 is what matters now
data.description:
After the Blue Wave swept across the US midterm elections with the Democrats winning control of both the House and Senate, OFFICIAL TRUMP [TRUMP] faced strong selling pressure.

The token dropped 17.37% to $1.27 in the last 24 hours and briefly hit a new all-time low of $1.22, despite the wider crypto market’s slight rally.

This sharp drop shows rising uncertainty about the future of President Trump’s crypto-friendly policies and the chance that Congress may look more closely at his family’s crypto activities.

The sell-off has also spread to other political memecoins, indicating that TRUMP isn’t the only token under scrutiny.

TRUMP’s daily chart shows little sign of a recovery

TRUMP’s daily chart continued to paint a bearish picture, with the token trading at $1.28 at the time of writing. Notably, the price remained within the 23.6% Fibonacci retracement zone, implying that the price has retraced most of its measured upward move.

As a result, bulls are left with little ground.

This continued weakness also raises questions about whether buyers can step in before the token loses the $1.22 level, which is becoming increasingly important for a potential recovery.

An RSI of 27.69 indicated that the recent decline puts TRUMP deep into the oversold territory, with sell pressure dominating. The slight uptick in OBV shows that buyers may be returning, giving the memecoin a glimmer of hope.

However, buying must continue for the price to hold above the key $1.22 level.

TRUMP’s 4-hour chart also looks bearish

The 4-hour chart shows little sign of a trend reversal. TRUMP is still in the 23.6% Fibonacci zone, and the RSI has dropped to 20, showing even stronger bearish momentum in the short term.

The OBV has also fallen sharply, which suggests buying volume is not keeping up with selling, and there is little sign of accumulation.

Final Summary

  • A break below $1.22 could see TRUMP under further pressure, especially if the buyers can’t continue to take the selling.
  • If buyers can claw back $1.30, then TRUMP may have some breathing space to consolidate before another attempt at a recovery up towards $1.50.

data.title: Is crypto’s 2026 outlook at risk as regulatory FUD returns to Washington?
data.description:
After the election, investors are looking for clues about crypto’s regulatory future.

However, one thing is clear: the road ahead remains uncertain, with volatility already creeping into the market. The impact of the recent election goes beyond the broader U.S. macro environment, extending into the regulatory landscape as well. The crypto industry has seen huge gains under Republican leadership in the U.S. with President Donald Trump’s vision of making the country the “crypto capital of the world.”

However, with Republicans holding a narrow majority in Congress, investors are becoming more cautious about what comes next. The recent challenges faced with the CLARITY Act, and the increased focus from the SEC around tokenizations, are adding to the uncertainty in the regulatory outlook.

That said, signs of a regulatory shift are already starting to emerge.

In the latest development, House Democrats are drafting a new bill regarding how crypto should be structured moving forward. The bill includes expanding the SEC’s jurisdiction and will also include provisions excluded from the CLARITY Act. This comes ahead of any potential change in who controls Congress.

From a regulatory standpoint, tighter SEC oversight could mean stricter compliance rules, increased scrutiny of crypto firms, and greater regulatory pressure on digital asset companies operating in the U.S. The key takeaway? Regulatory pressure may not stop at tighter SEC oversight.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, known to be a strong crypto critic, is expected to become the Chair of the Senate Banking Committee, potentially giving her greater influence over financial regulation and crypto policy.

Bitcoin risks deeper losses amid rising regulatory uncertainty

Is regulatory FUD shaping up to be the next major bearish catalyst for the broader crypto market?

The recent political upheaval in the U.S. Congress has already started to affect regulation. Discussions around a new crypto market structure bill, increasing anti-crypto sentiment and potential increased scrutiny from the SEC are adding a new layer of uncertainty to an already volatile market.

Further adding to the concern, Bitcoin [BTC] is looking bleak on its yearly chart. Historically, Bitcoin has never closed consecutive years in the red. However, this could change soon. Bitcoin is currently trading around 12% lower on its 2026 yearly candle, with just two months left before the year closes. This follows a red candle in 2025, putting BTC at risk of recording its first-ever back-to-back years of annual losses.

In essence, Bitcoin’s next move may depend on more than just market sentiment.

As regulatory uncertainty increases amid potential increased attention from the SEC, Bitcoin has another factor to contend with. If selling pressure continues, BTC could be heading toward its first-ever back-to-back annual losses, breaking a decade-long historical trend.

Final Summary

data.title: XRP bear trap alert! Bitfinex shorts surge 652% as supply tightens
data.description:
The current market breakdown could go either way. 

On one hand, this can lead to a further capitulation phase for the market as key support levels come under threat. However, it could also be seen as a bear trap for those short sellers who have stretched their positions too far. Notably, XRP seems to be at the forefront of this debate.

As the chart below shows, Bitfinex XRP shorts have spiked by 652.89% to 468.2 million. Given the weakening technical momentum, this bearish positioning is not entirely surprising. The altcoin has seen five straight  weekly lows and broken below the $1.20 support level, with its price now approaching the $1 mark.

Meanwhile, XRP’s relative strength is adding another layer of pressure. 

After breaking out of its five-week consolidation, the XRP/ETH pair has dropped over 3% this week. This indicates that XRP is losing value to Ethereum, as traders are showing preference towards ETH in this current bear trend. This relative weakness in XRP is therefore contributing to the bearish sentiment.

From a technical standpoint, betting on more Ripple [XRP] downside, with $1 as the next target, looks like a calculated move rather than a random bet. However, on-chain signals are telling a different story, keeping the possibility of a bear trap on the table.

XRP supply shock signals challenge bearish bets 

XRP is flashing textbook signs of a potential supply shock.

On the 5th of September, an estimated 13.24 million XRP was taken off exchanges, limiting the amount available to sell (as noted by one analyst). Moreover, whale holdings have increased by nearly 60 million XRP over the past week. While it is unclear whether these are the same tokens that left exchanges, both signals point to growing accumulation by large holders. 

The key takeaway? XRP’s Binance Scarcity Index has hit its highest level since 2022. As shown in the chart below, the index has been deeply negative throughout September and October before making a sharp move higher in recent days. The index is now extremely positive, and it is one of its largest movements in almost 4 years. This indicates that XRP supply is becoming tighter on Binance.

Ultimately, XRP is showing a clear split between its technical and on-chain signals. 

While negative momentum and increasing short interest indicate that there is more downside to come, market outflows, whale accumulation, and reduced Binance supply suggest that selling pressure may be losing steam. If these supply patterns remain, then those shorting the market hoping for a fall to $1 may be caught off guard, turning the current bearish setup into a potential bear trap. 

Final Summary

data.title: ‘Worst days in history’ – Trump’s stock-market reaction meets crypto’s $900B slide
data.description:
Bloodbath is the perfect word to describe the post-election market action.

Despite the markets trading on the assumption that Democrats will win, with odds hitting a high of 99%, crypto has suffered a severe sell-off. However, the downside may not be over yet. The total crypto market cap has now slipped back to mid-September levels, marking five straight weeks of losses and wiping out nearly $900 billion in market value.

The result? A textbook liquidity sweep. According to Coinglass, nearly $1 billion in positions were liquidated on the 5th of September, marking the largest single-day wipeout since the $2 billion short squeeze in mid-August. However, unlike that event, nearly 80% of the liquidations came from longs, showing that bullish traders were heavily caught offside as the market moved lower.

That said, the sell-off wasn’t just “crypto-specific.”

As the chart above shows, the Nasdaq 100 suffered its largest one-day loss since the pandemic, while the S&P500 lost $3 trillion in value. This comes just 24 hours after the Dow surged 1,600 points after Democrats swept the midterms. This indicates that there has been an abrupt change in sentiment post-election.

Notably, the U.S. President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to say that it is one of the stock market’s “worst days in history.” The crypto wipeout seems to be part of a wider correction in the market, with post-election volatility adding to the selling pressure. However, the move may not be just another election-driven pullback. The latest market data suggests there could be more going on beneath the surface.

Crypto faces fresh capitulation risks as market sentiment weakens

The market FUD seems to be less about the election itself and more about President Trump.

From a technical standpoint, this shift in sentiment makes sense. Crypto initially saw a strong boost from optimism around his election, but that momentum has since faded. However, the momentum has died out. Bitcoin [BTC] is currently down almost 30% from its peak of $126k despite progress made in regulation with the GENIUS Act, greater tokenization and increased adoption in stablecoins into traditional finance.

To add to the pressure, there are now reports that Trump Media sold a total of $343 million worth of Bitcoin. This adds to concerns regarding institutional selling and has also created more FUD around Trump, further weakening the bullish sentiment that initially drove crypto’s post-election rally.

Against this backdrop, crypto’s wipeout could be more than just a reaction to broader market weakness.

Besides the traditional markets digesting how the election will affect the AI space, there are further pressures on the crypto space. On top of reports that Trump Media is selling off its Bitcoin, there continue to be outflows from ETFs. In essence, crypto is facing its own market-specific headwinds.

In turn, crypto could be entering a more severe capitulation phase now that prices have retreated back to mid-September levels.

Final Summary

data.title: U.S. tech sell-off spills into crypto: Solana slides to $89.63 as AI spending fears mount
data.description:
Following the U.S. midterm elections, U.S. tech stocks experienced a sharp sell-off, especially after investors grew increasingly anxious over the political and economic landscape and questioned whether heavy capital flow into AI infrastructure could generate returns in the near term.

The Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, marking its biggest one-day loss in 18 months and making investors more cautious. This sell-off also affected the crypto market, with Solana [SOL] falling 6.86% to $89.63 in the last 24 hours.

What made the decline worse were concerns within the Solana ecosystem. Notably, lending protocol Loopscale stopped operations after a security issue, while an upcoming validator upgrade deadline created more uncertainty for the network.

At the same time, over $11 million in long SOL positions were liquidated in an hour, thus increasing the selling pressure.

Solana’s daily chart signals continued bearish pressure

At the time of writing, SOL was trading at $89.63, within the 23.6% Fibonacci level on the daily chart. This recent decline brought the token under serious pressure and close to its swing low of $88.48.

Momentum indicators were also in line with the bearish view. The MACD was clearly showing that the downward momentum was still very much intact and that the sellers were still in complete control of the broader price action.

That made it very difficult for the buyers to get any kind of sustained recovery.

However, the daily OBV showed a slight uptick following its sharp decline during the latest sell-off. While this could suggest that buying activity was beginning to return, the relatively flat movement offered little confirmation of anything meaningful.

For now, it suggested that buyers are fighting hard to defend the $88 level.

Is Solana entering a consolidation period?

AMBCrypto’s look at Solana’s 4-hour chart painted a clearer picture of the altcoin’s immediate price action. Notably, after declining into the 23.6% Fibonacci region, SOL began consolidating instead of extending its losses.

This suggested that even though buyers were attempting to defend the current price region, a convincing recovery remained elusive.

The MACD continued to highlight the token’s bearish momentum, indicating that the broader selling pressure had still not subsided entirely. OBV also trended downward, suggesting that selling activity continued to outweigh buying pressure on the shorter timeframe.

Both the daily and H4 suggested that SOL’s current consolidation would persist in the near term before a bullish reversal can start to form.

Furthermore, the $88.48 swing low is an important level to watch. If SOL manages to defend this region, it could continue consolidating or attempt a relief bounce. However, if lost, it would expose the token to further losses, with $85 being the next potential downside target.

Final Summary

  • Solana’s decline followed a broader risk-off move across financial markets, with weakness in U.S. technology stocks adding to selling pressure across crypto.
  • SOL’s daily and H4 charts continued to show bearish momentum, although the shorter-term consolidation could offer some relief if buyers defend the $88.48 region.

data.title: Polygon eyes hard fork to recover $6.5 mln in stolen POL – But at what cost?
data.description:
In a surprising development, Polygon has proposed a major network upgrade to recover approximately 70.49 million POL tokens, worth around $6.5 million. These were those tokens that were stolen during two separate security incidents involving Polymarket and Binance in October 2026.

The proposal aims to move the stolen tokens from five attacker-controlled wallets into recovery wallets designated by the compromised companies.

Remarking on which the team noted,

5 attacker-controlled addresses hold about 70.49M POL: about 23.86M POL (4 addresses) from the Polymarket incident and about 46.63M POL (1 address) from the Binance incident. The funds cannot move, but nothing in the current setup lets them be returned either.

Things Polygon needs to do

Polygon’s block producers have already added these addresses to their transaction blocklists. This they did to prevent the attackers from moving the funds further. However, this measure only freezes the assets, and it does not return them to their actual owners.

The existing system also requires block producers to restart their infrastructure whenever blocklist changes are made, making it difficult to maintain these restrictions over time.

Hence, to address this issue, Polygon has proposed a hard fork, which is a major network upgrade that changes the blockchain’s underlying rules.

Under the proposal, at a predetermined block, the POL balances of the five identified wallets would be reduced to zero. The same amounts would then be credited to recovery addresses verified and designated by Polymarket and Binance.

However, for this plan to succeed, the proposal also requires both companies to prove ownership of their designated recovery addresses before the upgrade. If approved, developers will first implement and test the changes on Polygon’s Amoy testnet before deploying them on mainnet.

At the same time, validators, exchanges, and node operators will also need to upgrade their software before activation.
However, the proposal has raised important questions about decentralization and user ownership.

The red flag in question

Normally, blockchain transactions cannot be reversed or wallet balances moved without the owner’s private keys. But Polygon’s proposed intervention would override this principle through a consensus-level change.

However, the network argued,

It is an extreme action that should not be reproduced commonly.

This comes as the Polygon’s MATIC was trading at $0.098 after a hike of 2.08% in the past 24 hours.

But with 21Shares recently withdrawing approximately $11 million worth of POL from Coinbase over the past 30 days, including 45.7 million POL worth $4.08 million on 28th October, concerns remain.

Final Summary

  • As of now, Polygon’s block producers have already added these addresses to their transaction blocklists.
  • But at the same time, the proposal has also raised important questions about decentralization and user ownership.
